belief: I cannot make it on my own.
origins: This belief can develop when a person was overprotected, never allowed to make decisions, or told they were incapable. It can also follow years of depending on a spouse, parent, or caregiver, or a loss that left someone suddenly alone. The belief is partly true, because we all need God and other people. It becomes harmful when it turns into fear of being alone, staying in unhealthy relationships, or giving up our own decisions.
teaches: Scripture honors healthy dependence. Two are better than one, and God settles the lonely in families. Our ultimate dependence is on the Lord, who holds our right hand and helps us. But the Bible also calls each person to carry his own load and to grow in maturity. Needing God and others does not mean you are helpless. God has given you abilities, judgment, and His Spirit. You can lean on Him and on safe people while also taking responsibility for your own life.
self_statements: I need someone to take care of me.
I can’t make decisions on my own.
If I lose this person, I’ll fall apart.
I’m not capable of running my life.
I’ll put up with anything rather than be alone.
Others know better than I do.
errors: Believing that if I need help with some things, I can’t do anything on my own.
Predicting that I will fail if I try to stand on my own.
Overlooking the things I already do well by myself.
Imagining that being alone would be unbearable.
questions: What do I already do on my own, even if I don’t notice it?
Who taught me that I couldn’t manage by myself?
Is there a difference between needing help and being helpless?
Am I staying in anything unhealthy because I fear being alone?
What does God say about His help and my responsibility?
What is one decision I can make myself this week?
truth: I need God, and I need people; that is how He made me. But needing help does not mean I am helpless. God holds my hand and has given me abilities and judgment. I can take responsibility for my life, make my own decisions, and still lean on Him and on safe people.
hw_truths: My help comes from the Lord.
Needing help is not the same as being helpless.
God has given me abilities and judgment.
I can make decisions and learn from them.
Healthy relationships are chosen, not clung to.
log: Things I did on my own
Each day, write one thing you handled or decided yourself, and how it went.
actions: Write down every task you already handle on your own. Include small things. Read the list when you feel helpless.
Choose one decision you would normally hand to someone else, make it, and notice what happens.
Pick one practical skill, such as paying a bill online or cooking a simple meal, and learn it this week.
Add one more safe person or group to your life so you are not relying on just one person.
prayer: Lord, I lean on You, and I thank You for the people You have given me. Help me see the abilities You have placed in me. Give me courage to take responsibility, make decisions, and grow, knowing You hold my hand. Amen.
